nodes.name: When Called
nodes.notes: ADR-053 Block 3 — Files-API input path. Inputs: input_images_json (JSON string of Read Input's image blocks [{type:image, ref, mime, source_ref, alt, order}] — also accepts {url} alias / {att_id}); clickup_task_id (for warning context). Caller (Stage B, Block 5) forwards Read Input's image-typed blocks. Test entry via scripts/test-subworkflow.mjs.

nodes.name: Get Anthropic Key
nodes.notes: Reads the anthropic_api_key Vault secret via SECURITY DEFINER getter public.get_anthropic_key() (migration 034). Code nodes can't use n8n credentials and $env/$vars are unavailable on this CE (CLAUDE.md), so a credentialed Postgres read is how a workflow obtains the secret. Returns {key} (null if unseeded). A hard DB failure throws -> errorWorkflow CRITICAL (reactive layer).

nodes.name: Parse Images
nodes.notes: Parse input_images_json -> image refs, embed the Anthropic key + task id into each element. Emits ONE item { key, clickup_task_id, images[], do_upload, key_missing, no_images }. do_upload=false when key unreachable OR no images -> rides the false branch to Merge as the no-work sentinel so the single terminal Aggregate still runs (mirrors Read Input's _passthrough). Splitting happens downstream via Split Out (itemList pairing), so $('Split Out Images').item recovers metadata after the fetch wipes $json.

nodes.name: Should Upload?
nodes.notes: true -> Split Out Images -> fetch+upload. false (no key OR no images) -> the single sentinel item rides to Merge (input 3) so Aggregate always runs and returns a well-formed empty map (+ key-unreachable WARN if the key was missing). main[1] is the IF false branch, not an error output.

nodes.name: Split Out Images
nodes.notes: Fan the images array into one item per image (itemList pairing). Each item = { ref, mime, source_ref, alt, order, key, clickup_task_id }. Downstream nodes recover metadata via $('Split Out Images').item.json after Fetch (responseFormat:file) replaces $json with response metadata (same idiom Read Input uses for Build Text Block).

nodes.name: Fetch Image Bytes
nodes.notes: GET the image ref to a binary property (no base64 in JSON; off-heap). ClickUp pre-signed and Supabase-signed URLs need no auth header. responseFormat:file. onError:continueErrorOutput -> a fetch failure (expired URL, 404, network) routes to Build Dropped Fetch -> WARN + drop, the block continues (silent-failure mode: un-fetchable image).

nodes.name: Prep Binary
nodes.notes: Ensure the binary part is well-formed for the Files-API multipart: set mimeType from Split Out's mime and a deterministic fileName when the fetch response omitted Content-Disposition (some signed URLs do). Mirrors Read Input's zip filename fixer. Runs once per item on the fetch-success branch only.

nodes.name: Upload to Files API
nodes.notes: POST /v1/files multipart (file part + purpose=agent) with anthropic-beta: files-api-2025-04-14 (Block 0 spec). Key sourced via paired item from Split Out (Code nodes can't read the cred). Returns {id:file_..., filename, mime_type, size_bytes, downloadable:false}. onError:continueErrorOutput -> upload failure (oversize 413, auth, network) routes to Build Dropped Upload -> WARN + drop; the task proceeds text-only rather than failing (silent-failure mode).

nodes.name: Build OK Entry
nodes.notes: Upload success -> map entry { ok:true, file_id, url(=input ref), source_ref, mime, alt, order }. The {file_id<->url} map Stage B carries into the session (the Agent Session contract's input_file_refs). alwaysOutputData so an empty input still emits (filtered by Aggregate) and the Merge append never stalls on an empty branch (Read Input note).

nodes.name: Build Dropped Fetch
nodes.notes: Fetch failure -> dropped entry { ok:false, warn_source:'files-api/fetch-failed', source_ref, err }. Aggregate turns it into a returned WARN. alwaysOutputData so the empty (no-failure) case still emits and the Merge append never stalls.

nodes.name: Build Dropped Upload
nodes.notes: Upload failure -> dropped entry { ok:false, warn_source:'files-api/upload-failed', source_ref, err }. Aggregate turns it into a returned WARN; the task proceeds text-only. alwaysOutputData so the empty case still emits and Merge append never stalls.

nodes.name: Merge
nodes.notes: Converge OK entries (0), dropped-fetch (1), dropped-upload (2), and the no-work sentinel (3, IF false) into ONE stream so Aggregate keeps a SINGLE input (a run-once-for-all-items node with N inputs runs once per connection and drops items — CLAUDE.md trap). Append = concat; tolerant of empty branches (same as Read Input's 5-input Merge, plus alwaysOutputData upstream).

nodes.name: Aggregate
nodes.notes: SOLE TERMINAL (single input via Merge -> branch-free deterministic return, CLAUDE.md). Returns { file_map:[{file_id,url,source_ref,mime,alt,order}], warnings:[{source,source_ref,err,severity}], clickup_task_id, uploaded_count, dropped_count }. Warnings are RETURNED, not fired — Stage B (Block 5) fires them via Post Alert (v1), mirroring Read Input -> Stage A. no_images is NOT a warning (legitimately no input images).

nodes.name: Upsert File Map
nodes.notes: ADR-055 Block 5.2: persist the file_id->{url,mime,source_ref} map to agent_input_file_map so the image MCP tool handler can resolve generate_image reference_file_ids -> signed URLs WITHOUT session context (Block 5.1). Additive + fail-soft: onError=continueRegularOutput + alwaysOutputData so a DB write failure NEVER blocks the upload return (Final Return re-reads Aggregate and appends a WARN). Empty file_map -> jsonb_to_recordset('[]') -> 0 rows -> no-op (the common no-input-images case). on conflict refreshes url/mime/source_ref.

nodes.name: Final Return
nodes.notes: SOLE TERMINAL (return-determinism idiom, CLAUDE.md). Re-reads Aggregate's canonical output {file_map, warnings, clickup_task_id, uploaded_count, dropped_count} so the agent_input_file_map write side-effect can't corrupt the return. Appends an agent-input-file-map/write-failed WARN (returned for Stage B to fire) if the upsert errored — a failed map write silently degrades later reference resolution, so it must surface.
